lines: // ClientRequest.setTimeout will be fired on the specify milliseconds, and can make sure that abort() will be fired after connect.
-        var timeoutErrorMessage = config.timeout ? 'timeout of ' + config.timeout + 'ms exceeded' : 'timeout exceeded';

content.text:
I fixed it: when a request times out in Node.js, axios now uses `config.timeoutErrorMessage` if one is set. If it isn't set, you still get the usual `timeout of <n>ms exceeded`. I haven't run any tests, including the repro from the issue.

The change is in the timeout handler in `lib/adapters/http.js` (around line 421). Requests in Node.js go through that file, and it always built the default message without checking `timeoutErrorMessage`. The error code didn't change: it's still `ECONNABORTED`, or `ETIMEDOUT` when `clarifyTimeoutError` is on.
